questions.q: Which button in the designer opens the full expression editor for an input field?
options: The fx button
The gear/settings icon
The lightning bolt button
The Save button on the command bar
questions.explain: The lightning bolt inserts dynamic content directly. The fx button opens the expression editor, with Function and Dynamic content tabs.

questions.q: What is the structure of every Power Automate expression?
options: A connector name followed by a colon and a value
A trigger name followed by a condition
A table name followed by a column reference
A function name followed by parentheses containing its arguments
questions.explain: Expressions follow functionName(argument1, argument2, ...) syntax. Functions can nest inside one another's arguments.

questions.q: In the expression addDays(utcNow(), 7), what does utcNow() do?
options: It schedules the flow to run seven days from now
It returns the current date and time in UTC, which is then fed into addDays() as its starting timestamp
It is a typo and has no function in Power Automate
It converts a date to Universal Coordinated format for storage
questions.explain: utcNow() returns the current UTC date and time. Because it's nested inside addDays(), its result becomes addDays()'s first argument, and 7 days get added to it.

questions.q: Besides typing a function name directly, what's the shortcut way to open the dynamic content and expression editor popup from inside an input field?
options: Typing a forward slash (/) in the field
Right-clicking the field and choosing Insert
There is no shortcut; you must always click the fx button
Pressing Ctrl+Shift+E
questions.explain: Typing a forward slash in an input field opens the same dynamic content and expression editor popup as clicking the lightning bolt or fx buttons.

questions.q: A Castlebridge Logistics flow needs to turn a trigger's submitted date into a three-business-day-later, human-readable deadline in one step. What expression pattern accomplishes this?
options: A single nested expression: formatDateTime(addDays(submittedDate, 3), 'dddd, MMMM d')
A Condition action checking if the date is a weekday
Three separate Compose actions chained with Set variable
concat(submittedDate, '+3 days')
questions.explain: Nesting addDays() inside formatDateTime() lets one expression both shift the date forward and format it as readable text, read from the inside out.
